elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.6 proviso now runs to PB alone: "provided, however, that PB may assign, sublicense or transfer this Agreement and all of its rights and obligations hereunder, in their entirety, to any of its Affiliates ..." — a no-consent affiliate transfer right for PB (Customer).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same PB-only proviso continues: "or to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise".

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The general bar is retained ("Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto ... neither Party will sell, transfer, assign, pledge or otherwise dispose of ... this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder") and the former mutual ("either Party") carve-out is narrowed to PB, so SFJ can no longer assign — even to Affiliates or a successor — without PB's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted parenthetical in 15.6: "(which consent, in the case of an assignment by SFJ, will not be unreasonably withheld)" — correct party direction (PB's consent to an SFJ assignment).

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "SFJ shall not at any time sell, assign, sublicense or otherwise transfer this Agreement to an entity whose primary business is the development or commercialization of pharmaceutical or biotechnology products." The Program Transfer sunset sentence is deleted and the PB sole-discretion consent gate is replaced by an absolute, permanent bar covering PB's competitor space.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2.6: "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB." The former sole-discretion termination right and the 150% Development Costs payment triggered by it are removed; heading changed to "Change of Control of PB".

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor/affiliate carve-out is now PB-only; SFJ's ability to assign to a successor is subject to PB's prior written consent, so the fallback's mutual successor right is absent (this is deliberate, since the preferred level is targeted).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears in rendered 15.6; PB's affiliate/successor transfers are permitted with no written-notice obligation.
PB retains a no-consent, non-successor exception (transfers "to any of its Affiliates"), which under the ASSIGN fallback boundary defeats a clean "other assignments require consent" result.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is expressly limited to "an assignment by SFJ"; PB's non-carve-out assignments remain subject to SFJ's consent with no stated standard.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (PB affiliate/successor carve-out retained and made unilateral, SFJ assignment gated on PB consent not unreasonably withheld, permanent competitor bar, express removal of SFJ's change-of-control termination right). Fallback is not met, which is acceptable because the higher level is complete.

Minimality defect in 14.2.6: the drafter kept a rewritten residual sentence — "PB shall remain obligated to pay any Approval Payments that become due and payable pursuant to ARTICLE 6 in accordance with ARTICLE 6." No selected element requires it, and it merely duplicates Article 6's existing payment machinery. Fix: delete this sentence so 14.2.6 reads only the notice sentence plus "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB."

If that residual sentence is retained, it also silently drops PB-favourable qualifiers from the original text — "(except to the extent of the amount of any Buy-Out Payment paid by PB pursuant to Section 6.7)" and "provided that such Approval Payments (or Buy-Out Payment, as applicable) shall be adjusted as set forth in Section 6.2". Removing Customer-favourable words outside the chosen elements fails minimality; restore them verbatim or delete the sentence entirely.

Consequential deletions inside 14.2.6 (the 150% Development Costs payment, the SFJ purchase of the Trial Data Package, and the post-termination Commercially Reasonable Effort covenant) are acceptable because each was expressly conditioned on "In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.6" and cannot survive removal of the termination right.

Intent is preserved on the face of the rendered text: the general mutual consent bar, PB's carve-outs, and SFJ's separate right to assign Approval Payment receipts to its limited partners (the trailing "and ..." text) are untouched, and Article 6 continues to govern Approval Payments including any Section 6.2 change-of-control adjustment and Section 6.7 buy-out credit.

Cross-reference sweep required before sending: confirm that Section 11.1.1.4 (Trial Data Package purchase), the Change of Control Buy-Out Payment definition/Section 6.7, and any survival or termination-consequences list do not cross-refer to "termination pursuant to Section 14.2.6". Any such reference becomes dangling once the termination right is deleted and must be conformed in the same redline.
